_authoring_conventions.note: Not part of the schema; documents the JSON shape this package chose where docs/schema/story-package.md leaves entry_state/exit_state as opaque JSON. See fixtures/authoring-notes.md for why.
_authoring_conventions.entry_state_and_exit_state: { <entity_id>: { <column>: <value>, ... }, ... } — one object per touched entity, naming only the core columns this scene asserts. Untouched entities are omitted, not restated.
_authoring_conventions.new_rows_in_exit_state: A scene that creates a new relationship or character_knowledge row (not just updates an existing entity's column) lists it under reserved keys _new_relationships / _new_character_knowledge inside exit_state, using the same row shape as world_model_seed.relationships / character_knowledge.

bag.role: carries the glass slipper on the Prince's order

bag.description: the family's rooms, where the sisters dress and hold court
the cinder-heap by the kitchen hearth where Cinderella is sent to sleep
holds the pumpkin bed, the mouse-trap, the rat-trap, and the watering-pot behind which the lizards live
abstracts the gentleman-in-waiting's circuit from house to house with the slipper

objects.name: a gown of gold and silver cloth, all beset with jewels

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establish the household inversion: a remarriage brings in a proud stepmother and two vain stepdaughters who demote Cinderella to servant status.
required_beats: the father has remarried a proud and haughty woman
her two daughters prove as haughty as their mother
the stepmother turns all the housework over to Cinderella and sends her to sleep in the chimney-corner
invariants: Cinderella performs all the housework without complaint
the father is established as unable or unwilling to intervene

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Introduce the external engine of the plot — the King's son gives a ball — and establish that Cinderella is not considered a possible guest.
required_beats: word arrives that the King's son is giving a ball, and all persons of fashion are invited
the two sisters are overjoyed and think of nothing but what to wear
Cinderella is expected to help them dress but is not imagined as a guest herself
invariants: Cinderella is not invited and does not protest

scene_cards.dramatic_function: A humiliation beat that sets the emotional stakes for the wish that follows.
required_beats: Cinderella dresses her sisters' hair with skill and good nature, since she has excellent taste
the sisters jeer that it would make people laugh to see a Cinderwench at a ball
Cinderella does not ask to go
invariants: Cinderella shows no resentment toward her sisters in front of them

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Isolate Cinderella and motivate the wish that the godmother answers.
required_beats: the stepmother and sisters depart for the ball
left alone, Cinderella weeps

scene_cards.dramatic_function: The turn: magical enablement bound by an explicit, load-bearing condition. Plants the midnight rule.

obj_rat.name: a fat coachman with the finest moustachios

required_beats: the godmother appears and asks why Cinderella weeps
a pumpkin is turned into a golden coach; six mice into horses; a rat into a coachman; six lizards into footmen
Cinderella's rags become a gown of gold and silver, beset with jewels, and a pair of glass slippers
the godmother warns her in plain terms: if she stays one moment past midnight, coach, horses, footmen, and gown will all revert
invariants: the transformation is witnessed by no one but Cinderella and the godmother
the midnight condition is stated aloud, not merely implied

scene_cards.dramatic_function: The court sees a beauty it cannot place; the Prince's attention turns to her; her own family fails to recognize her. Opens the irony gap that scene 9 will pay off.
required_beats: a hush falls and the dancing stops as she enters
the old King himself remarks on her beauty
the King's son leads her out to dance
no one — including her own stepmother and sisters — recognizes her
invariants: Cinderella's stepfamily gives no sign of recognizing her

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Demonstrate her wit and generosity in disguise, and establish the safe pattern of leaving in good time — the calm before scene 10 breaks it.
required_beats: Cinderella sits with her sisters and shares the oranges and citrons the Prince gave her
the sisters do not know her
she leaves at a quarter to twelve, well ahead of the deadline, and thanks the King and the Prince for their civility
she reaches home safely, with time to spare
invariants: nothing is lost or left behind this night

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Close the loop on night one and set up her wanting to go again — low-key connective tissue, not a discovery scene.
required_beats: Cinderella thanks her godmother
she confesses she would be glad to go to the ball again the next night
the godmother agrees to send her again

scene_cards.dramatic_function: The irony-gap centerpiece: the sisters describe the mystery princess to Cinderella's own face, certain she cannot possibly know who they mean.
required_beats: the sisters return home and can talk of nothing but the beautiful unknown princess at the ball
Cinderella asks the princess's name; the sisters say they do not know it
Cinderella asks, with feigned idle curiosity, to borrow Miss Charlotte's yellow suit so she might see the ball for herself
she is refused and mocked for the suggestion, as expected
scene_cards.tone: layered — comic on the surface, quietly charged underneath
invariants: the sisters give no sign of recognizing Cinderella as the princess
Cinderella gives no sign that she was there

scene_cards.dramatic_function: The midnight condition detonates. The plant from scene 5 pays off in the loss of one slipper and the total reversal of the magic.
required_beats: Cinderella returns for the second ball, more beautifully dressed than before
she is so happy she loses all track of time
she hears the clock begin to strike twelve and flees the hall at once
in her haste she loses one glass slipper on the palace steps
the Prince picks up the slipper she left behind, having failed to catch her
at the last stroke of midnight, coach, horses, coachman, footmen, and gown all revert to a pumpkin, mice, a rat, lizards, and rags
invariants: exactly one slipper is recovered by the Prince; the other leaves with Cinderella
the reversal is total except for the retained slipper

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Plants the second chain: proof survives the reversal, hidden. Mirrors the schema's own worked example of a possession created here and read back at the fitting.
required_beats: Cinderella arrives home on foot, in her old clothes, out of breath
of all her finery, only the fellow glass slipper remains, kept in her pocket
she says nothing of the ball to anyone in the household
invariants: no one else in the household learns she still has a slipper

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Raise the stakes across the kingdom before the search narrows onto the true owner. An omniscient-narration beat the nominal protagonist isn't present for — see authoring-notes.md.
required_beats: the Prince has it proclaimed by trumpet that he will marry whichever lady's foot fits the glass slipper
the slipper is tried on princesses, then duchesses, then all the ladies of the court, in vain
the search reaches at last the house of Cinderella's father
scene_cards.tone: expectant, almost farcical in its futility

scene_cards.dramatic_function: The recognition scene: both plants pay off together — the fit itself, and the produced fellow slipper.
required_beats: the sisters try the slipper in vain, squeezing and forcing their feet
Cinderella asks if she may try, and is laughed at
the gentleman-in-waiting says he has orders to let every maiden try, and looks earnestly at Cinderella, finding her very beautiful
the slipper goes onto her foot with perfect ease
Cinderella draws the fellow slipper from her pocket and puts it on
the godmother appears and touches Cinderella's clothes with her wand, turning them richer than ever before, in full view of the sisters this time
invariants: the slipper fits no one else who tries it
this transformation, unlike scene 5's, is witnessed openly by the stepfamily

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Resolution: mercy extended, the household's inversion undone in Cinderella's favor rather than avenged.
required_beats: the two sisters fling themselves at Cinderella's feet and beg pardon for all their ill usage of her
Cinderella forgives them freely and embraces them, and says she loves them with all her heart
she is taken to the palace and presented to the Prince, lovelier than ever
they are married within a few days
Cinderella, as good as she is beautiful, lodges her sisters in the palace and that same day marries them to two great lords of the court
invariants: Cinderella takes no revenge on her stepfamily

voice_card.narrative_distance: omniscient but close-focused on Cinderella; steps back only for scene 12's circuit of the kingdom
voice_card.register: plain, warmly ironic, folk-narrator; understates cruelty and wonder alike
voice_card.sentence_rhythm: short declarative sentences; occasional triads (rule-of-three lists — the pumpkin, the mice, the rat; princesses, duchesses, all the court)
voice_card.dialogue_density: low to moderate; the narrator reports more than it stages, with dialogue reserved for the sharpest lines (the sisters' jeers, the godmother's warning)
voice_card.style_exemplar: The cinders did not care that she was beautiful; they only made her so, night after night, until one night they didn't.

metadata.title: Cinderella, or the Little Glass Slipper
metadata.source: Andrew Lang (ed.), The Blue Fairy Book, Longmans, Green & Co., 1889 (Project Gutenberg #503; itself credited by Lang to Charles Perrault, 1697) — no Disney-derived material; see fixtures/authoring-notes.md for the copyright-hygiene check
